current_example.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $g(x) = 3 x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $3.$
current_example.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}3x\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{c}^{2}}{2}-0) \\ 3 & =\frac{3c}{2} \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$
